facts.raw_span: born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
weighing 2152 g
one of monochorionic diamniotic twins
her identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound had shown microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI of the head revealed microcephaly, marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles without signs of elevated intracranial pressure
severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum were preserved
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions were seen
very weak light reflexes bilaterally
mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign
No chorioretinal dysplasia was noted

concepts.why: Fetal ultrasound and postnatal MRI showed microcephaly and ventricular enlargement, consistent with fetal brain disruption sequence.
Very weak light reflexes and mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign are consistent with optic nerve hypoplasia.
Fetal ultrasound and postnatal MRI showed ventricular enlargement, which may be related to periventricular leukomalacia.
Very weak light reflexes and mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign are consistent with cerebral visual impairment.
It explains the preservation of certain brain structures and the absence of chorioretinal dysplasia.

rationales.F03: Monochorionic diamniotic twins suggest a possible shared placental circulation issue, which could contribute to fetal brain disruption sequence.
rationales.F04: The death of the identical twin in utero could have led to a disruption in placental circulation, potentially affecting the development of the surviving twin's brain.
rationales.F05: Fetal ultrasound findings of microcephaly and ventricular enlargement are consistent with fetal brain disruption sequence.
rationales.F06: Postnatal MRI findings of microcephaly and marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles support the diagnosis of fetal brain disruption sequence.
rationales.F07: Severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes is a characteristic feature of fetal brain disruption sequence.
rationales.F10: Very weak light reflexes bilaterally could indicate optic nerve hypoplasia or cerebral visual impairment.
rationales.F11: Mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign is consistent with optic nerve hypoplasia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The combination of microcephaly, ventricular enlargement, and severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, along with the history of monochorionic diamniotic twins and in utero death of the identical twin, strongly supports Fetal brain disruption sequence as the most likely diagnosis.
